summary:
Held 1 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 5 upside misses — IP +11%, SW +11%, DLR +11%, PKG +9%, NOW +7%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (SNDK -11%, COHR -10%, CHRW -9%, LITE -8%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: IP (+11.21%) — Cluster of bullish sell-side moves ahead of Jul 30 earnings — RBC hiked PT to $48, Truist to $46 — citing tightening containerboard supply after mill outages/capacity cuts and rising linerboard prices. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe — IP is a large-cap paper/packaging industrial, a sector the bot's momentum/tech-leaning universes typically exclude. Move was a multi-day analyst-target grind-up, not a single sharp gap/volume spike a news-reactive scanner would flag.

top_movers.catalyst: Cluster of bullish sell-side moves ahead of Jul 30 earnings — RBC hiked PT to $48, Truist to $46 — citing tightening containerboard supply after mill outages/capacity cuts and rising linerboard prices.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — IP is a large-cap paper/packaging industrial, a sector the bot's momentum/tech-leaning universes typically exclude. Move was a multi-day analyst-target grind-up, not a single sharp gap/volume spike a news-reactive scanner would flag.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a paper/packaging & basic-materials bucket to universe inclusion rules, and add a signal for clustered sell-side PT hikes (≥2 upgrades raising target >8% within 5 trading days) to catch pre-earnings analyst-driven runs.

top_movers.catalyst: Multiple analyst price-target hikes (JPMorgan to $65, Citi/RBC to $56, Truist to $55) plus bullish packaging-demand sentiment ahead of July 29 Q2 earnings drove a pre-print momentum run.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — SW is a mid/large-cap industrial packaging name (Irish-domiciled NYSE plc), a sector/geography likely not covered by momentum or news-reactive universes tuned to tech/domestic large-caps.
top_movers.suggestion: Add industrials/materials packaging names above a market-cap floor (e.g. >$20B) to the momentum universe, with an analyst-revision trigger (≥3 PT raises in 30 days) to catch pre-earnings drift like this.

top_movers.catalyst: Q2 2026 earnings beat (EPS $0.55 vs $0.51 est, revenue $8.97B vs $8.76B est) with FCF surge and Q3 guidance for margin expansion; shares extended their post-earnings pop through Monday's close.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — SLB is a mega-cap oilfield-services/energy name, a sector/cap bucket the bot's momentum and mean-reversion strategies aren't scoped to trade, so the earnings gap was never evaluated by them.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap energy/oilfield-services names (e.g. SLB, HAL, BKR) to the momentum strategy's tradable universe, or add an earnings-gap release rule (post-results gap ≥8% within first 30min) that lets excluded-sector names in temporarily.

top_movers.catalyst: Q2 earnings crushed estimates (rev $1.92B vs $1.67B est, core FFO guide raised to $8.15-8.20) on 7/23; cascading analyst PT hikes (TD Cowen, JPMorgan, RBC, Deutsche Bank, Barclays) extended the AI/data-center-demand rally into 7/27.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — DLR sits in the GICS Real Estate/data-center REIT bucket, which momentum and news-reactive equity strategies likely exclude via a sector filter (REITs trade on FFO/cap-rate dynamics, not EPS, so they're screened out of earnings-surprise scans).
top_movers.suggestion: Carve out a data-center REIT allowlist (DLR, EQIX, DBRG) inside the sector exclusion so post-earnings gap-ups ≥5% with FFO-beat + guidance raise still route to the earnings-momentum sleeve instead of being blocked outright.

top_movers.catalyst: Q2 2026 EPS beat ($2.35 vs $2.31 est) on record corrugated shipments, plus a $140/ton containerboard price hike announced for Sep 2026 boosting the demand/pricing outlook.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — PKG is a large-cap industrial/paper-packaging name, a sector the bot's universes likely don't cover (no materials/packaging bucket configured), so no filter ever got a chance to evaluate it.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a materials/industrial-packaging sector bucket (or a generic S&P mid/large-cap earnings-gap scanner) to at least one strategy's universe so post-earnings gappers like PKG become visible pre-open.

top_movers.catalyst: Q2 earnings beat (rev +24% YoY) w/ raised FY guidance and AI ACV >$1B (reported 7/22); rally extended into 7/27 on follow-on analyst price-target hikes.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — NOW is a mega-cap enterprise-SaaS name outside sector/cap coverage; today's pop is day-3 post-earnings drift (earnings 7/22), not a fresh gap a day-of scanner would flag.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap enterprise-software names to universe, or add a post-earnings-drift rescreen checking names 2-5 sessions after a beat+guide-raise, not just day-of gap-ups.

top_movers.catalyst: No single company-specific news; sector-wide memory/NAND selloff plus profit-taking ahead of Aug 5 earnings, amplified by Chinese rival ChangXin Technology's blowout IPO (+466%) stoking NAND/DRAM competition fears.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — likely excluded as a recent WDC spinoff with a still-short trading history and an unusually high nominal share price (~$1,436), traits that typically fail cap/liquidity or price-band universe screens.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a post-spinoff onboarding rule that admits names into the universe once they clear ~12 months of trading history and pass standard liquidity checks, rather than gating purely on price-per-share or ticker age.

top_movers.catalyst: No firm-specific news; COHR fell with peers (Lumentum, Applied Optoelectronics, Ciena) in a broad profit-taking unwind of the crowded AI-optics/photonics trade ahead of its Aug 12 earnings.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — COHR sits in a niche photonics/optical-components sub-sector the bot's tech universes don't track, so no strategy had it on watch when the sector-wide de-rating hit.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a 'photonics/optical-components' watchlist (COHR, LITE, AAOI, CIEN, FN) to the sector-momentum universe so correlated AI-optics unwinds trigger a signal instead of being invisible.

top_movers.catalyst: Sector-wide freight-broker selloff on AI-disruption fears (rival freight-matching tech claims ~70% cut in empty miles), not CHRW-specific news — RXO -18%, EXPD -13%, LSTR -10% moved in sympathy.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — CHRW is a mid/large-cap logistics/freight-brokerage services name, a sector likely excluded from tech- or momentum-focused universes; also a thematic multi-name sector rotation rather than a single-stock gap/news event a catalyst scanner would key on.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a sector-rotation flag that screens for ≥3 same-subindustry peers moving >5% same session (e.g., transportation/logistics GICS group) and temporarily admits them to the tradable universe for mean-reversion/momentum evaluation.

top_movers.catalyst: No fresh company-specific news — LITE fell with the broader AI-photonics/optics complex (also hit Coherent, AOI) amid renewed AI-capex jitters after OpenAI IPO-delay reports, compounding recent Russell-index-removal selling pressure.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — LITE is a high-beta optical-components/photonics name only added to the S&P 500 in March 2026; the bot's universe list likely wasn't refreshed to include this recent index entrant or excludes the comms-equipment/photonics sector entirely.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a monthly S&P 500/Russell reconstitution sync job to auto-ingest new index additions (like LITE's March 2026 inclusion) into strategy universes instead of relying on a static ticker list.
